subject: Insurance
title: Flood Insurance Failures
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Flood Insurance Failures.

hook.text: FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program is $20.5 billion in debt.

buildup.text: NFIP was created in 1968 because private insurers wouldn't cover flood risk.

discovery.text: Some properties have flooded 40+ times while paying only modest premiums. The program subsidizes chronic flood risk.

twist.text: Risk Rating 2.0 updated NFIP pricing in 2021 to reflect actual risk.

climax.text: Accurate pricing makes insurance unaffordable for many.

quiz.question: Why is FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program in debt?
options: It charges below-market rates for properties that flood repeatedly
